correctness.rationale: For a zero-sum unit quadruple in a strictly convex normed plane, the two unit pairs with the same sum correspond to the intersection of the unit sphere with a nonzero translate of itself. A horizontal-section proof shows that two such strictly convex planar boundaries have at most two common points, so the pairs coincide and the quadruple is antipodal after relabelling. The six-distance energy therefore equals \(8+2\|x+y\|^2+2\|x-y\|^2\), yielding \(8+8C'_{\mathrm{NJ}}(X)\). Ciesielski--Płuciennik Theorem 2 specialized to \(n=2\) gives \(C'_{\mathrm{NJ}}(\ell_p^2)=2^{|2/p-1|}\) for \(1<p<\infty\). The two endpoints attain the universal bound \(24\) by explicit four-vertex configurations. The numerical stress test is corroborative only.

value.rationale: The four-point invariant was introduced to capture inscribed-quadrilateral geometry, while its relation to classical two-point constants was previously only one-sided. Showing exact collapse on every strictly convex normed plane identifies a structural reason that the four-variable optimization simplifies and immediately yields the complete canonical \(\ell_p^2\) profile. This is a natural class-level theorem with a sharp parameter family, not a renaming, arbitrary slice, or table recomputation.
